newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bankers Trust calls Alphatec bondholders meeting.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust calls Alphatec bondholders meeting.

text.p: Thailand's Alphatec Electronics Plc eurobond holders have been called to a meeting on August 4-8 in Zurich, Switzerland by the bond's trustee Bankers Trust, Alphatec said in a statement on Tuesday.
The ailing Thai firm failed to meet a July 7 payment deadline to bondholders who on June 22 exercised a put option on $43.68 million of the firm's total $45 million euroconvertible, the firm said.

Bankers Trust's decision to call a meeting, not a default on the bond, means Alphatec does not have to make a payment -- at least until bondholders have met and decided what to do, the statement said.

Alphatec's failure to meet the payment comes as creditors and the firm battle over the company's restructuring plans, analysts said. Foreign creditors want high level changes within Alphatec's management team, which the current board is unwilling to make, they said.
A decline in the Thai stock market, which has dropped to more than eight-year lows this year, has found the electronics and semiconductor manufacturer facing a funding crisis.
U.S. electronics firm Texas Instruments pulled out of joint ventures with the firm in May citing Alphatec's difficulty in raising finance.
The firm has recently appealed to the Thai government for assistance but its requests have so far fallen on deaf ears.
